events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 8 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning and High Surf Warning, until noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon Thursday to 9 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Faria Beach to Silver Strand Beach), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers (including Ventura Pier) and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking waves may impact Ventura and Channel Islands Harbors. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An extreme high tide of around 8.1 feet will peak between 9 AM and 10 AM Thursday morning.

location.region: Ventura County Beaches

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 2:14PM PST until November 28 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 8 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 11 feet with
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning and High Surf Warning,
until noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon
Thursday to 9 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Faria
Beach to Silver Strand Beach), roads, and structures.
Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and
strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean
drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Ventura Pier) and jetties. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore. Large breaking waves may impact
Ventura and Channel Islands Harbors. Extremely high tides may
cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas
inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An extreme high tide of around 8.1 feet
will peak between 9 AM and 10 AM Thursday morning.
weather.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 8 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until noon PST today. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon today to 9 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Faria Beach to Silver Strand Beach), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers (including Ventura Pier) and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking waves may impact Ventura and Channel Islands Harbors. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An extreme high tide of around 8.1 feet will peak between 9 AM and 10 AM Thursday morning.

weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov/wfo/ilm .

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1000 PM EST.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.4 feet will peak near 11 AM Friday morning.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15
feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.4
feet will peak near 11 AM Friday morning.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.7 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft. * WHERE...The Pacific Coast. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Saturday morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 12:31 PM Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

location.region: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 1:31AM PST until November 28 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.7 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft.

* WHERE...The Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Saturday
morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at
12:31 PM Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM
Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM
Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current. * WHERE...Northern to eastern beaches of Puerto Rico and Culebra. * WHEN...Through Sunday morning. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.

location.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Culebra

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 27 at 6:59PM AST until November 29 at 8:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...Northern to eastern beaches of Puerto Rico and Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.
weather.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Culebra

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.2 feet will peak between 11 AM and Noon Saturday morning.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.2 feet will peak between 11 AM and Noon Saturday morning.

weather.description:

For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10
feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.

increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.2
feet will peak between 11 AM and Noon Saturday morning.

such conditions, stay off the rocks.

Low clouds will quickly become dense fog shortly after sunset. Be aware that dense fog will be widespread by late this evening, if you are traveling.

locations will experience zero visibility for several hours. This
dense fog event will be a Level 4 on a scale of 1 to 5.

* WHEN...From 8 PM this evening to Noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dense fog will make driving conditions hazardous leading

sunset. Be aware that dense fog will be widespread by late this

weather.instruction:

of distance ahead of you. Consider leaving after the dense fog has
gone. Be sure to change your headlights from AUTO to MANUAL, since
automatic headlights will not activate in the dense fog.

events.title: Beach Hazards Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.7 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft. * WHERE...The Pacific Coast. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through 6 AM Saturday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.description: * WHAT...High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. High tide is at 1:44 PM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge and 1:15 PM at the Arena Cove tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay including parks and roads with only isolated closures expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon.

events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... River levels are forecast to begin a very slow decline within Major flood stage this weekend and through next week. For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. The river crest has surpassed its previous flood of record. * WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney. * WHEN...Until further notice. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 13.1 feet. - Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 13.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain within Major Flood Stage. A slow decline from 13.1 feet may begin over the weekend into early next week. - Flood stage is 8.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

.Rainfall working through the basin has caused river levels on the
St. Johns Above Lake Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood
Stage, above its previous record flood stage. River levels are
forecast to begin a very slow decline within Major flood stage this
weekend and through next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river crest has surpassed its previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 13.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 13.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain within Major Flood
Stage. A slow decline from 13.1 feet may begin over the weekend
into early next week.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 900 PM EST.

weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Massachusetts...

Taunton River Near Bridgewater affecting Bristol and Plymouth
Counties.

For the Taunton River...including Bridgewater...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Taunton River near Bridgewater.

* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Backwater flooding from the Taunton River
will cause flooding of lower Purchade Brook in Middleboro.  This
will cause Woloski Park to become impassable by most vehicles.
Beware of the dangers of crossing flooded roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:45 AM EST Saturday the stage was 8.3 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:45 AM EST Saturday was 8.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.4 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late tomorrow
evening.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 600 PM EST.

profile vehicles. Plumes of blowing dust may create pockets of low

weather.instruction:
Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location prior to
the onset of winds.

Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Blowing dust can significantly lower air quality and it is encouraged
that you take preventative measures such as staying indoors or
wearing protective breathing masks if outside. High dust
concentrations can cause respiratory problems, decrease lung
activity, aggravate asthma, and lead to potential heart-related
problems, especially with children, elderly or those with
pre-existing respiratory conditions.

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...Life-threatening rip current. * WHERE...Northern and eastern beaches of Puerto Rico and Culebra. * WHEN...Through Sunday morning. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.

location.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Culebra

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 28 at 3:34AM AST until November 29 at 8:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...Northern and eastern beaches of Puerto Rico and
Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.
weather.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Culebra

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 27 at 11:13PM PST until November 28 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 PM PST Friday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:30 PM PST Friday was 17.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall below flood stage just after
midnight tonight to 16.0 feet late tonight. It will then rise to
16.3 feet late Sunday morning. It will fall to 16.1 feet late
Sunday evening. It will then rise above flood stage early Monday
morning to 16.8 feet late Monday evening. It will fall below
flood stage again Tuesday morning.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 16.8
feet on 03/13/2003.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 1000 AM PST.
